title: Acute kidney injury (adult)
subject: nephrology
summary: Diagnose and stage AKI with KDIGO creatinine and urine output criteria, find the prerenal, renal or postrenal cause, restore volume with buffered crystalloid, stop nephrotoxins, and start dialysis for life-threatening complications refractory to medical therapy.

sections.title: Definition and KDIGO staging
items: AKI: serum creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL (26.5 micromol/L) or more within 48 hours, OR rise to 1.5 times baseline or more known or presumed within the prior 7 days, OR urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 hours or more.
Stage 1: creatinine 1.5 to 1.9 times baseline or a rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more; urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 to 12 hours.
Stage 2: creatinine 2.0 to 2.9 times baseline; urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/h for 12 hours or more.

Stage 3: creatinine 3.0 times baseline or more, OR creatinine 4.0 mg/dL (353.6 micromol/L) or more, OR start of kidney replacement therapy; urine output below 0.3 mL/kg/h for 24 hours or more, or anuria for 12 hours or more.

Use the most recent stable pre-illness creatinine as baseline. The KDIGO 2026 draft adds cystatin C and damage biomarkers, calls AKI lasting more than 48 hours persistent, and uses acute kidney disease (AKD) for dysfunction lasting up to 3 months.

Classify the cause: prerenal (hypovolaemia, sepsis, cardiorenal, hepatorenal, NSAIDs, RAS blockers), intrinsic (acute tubular injury, interstitial nephritis, glomerulonephritis, vascular) or postrenal (obstruction).

sections.title: First steps
items: Check potassium, bicarbonate (venous gas) and a 12-lead ECG at once; treat hyperkalaemia first (see Hyperkalaemia protocol) and look for pulmonary oedema.
Assess volume status: capillary refill, JVP, postural BP, lung crackles or lung ultrasound B-lines, fluid balance and weight trend.

Hypovolaemia: give buffered crystalloid (Ringer lactate or Plasma-Lyte) rather than 0.9% saline, in boluses with reassessment after each; avoid starches, gelatin and albumin as first-line. Target MAP above 65 mmHg, adding a vasopressor if fluids alone fail.

Stop or hold nephrotoxins and volume-depleting drugs: NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, avoidable iodinated contrast, and temporarily ACE inhibitor, ARB, diuretics, metformin and SGLT2 inhibitor while acutely unwell.
Exclude obstruction early: bladder scan or urinary catheter for retention, and renal ultrasound, urgently if pyonephrosis, a single kidney or bilateral obstruction is possible.
Dose all renally cleared drugs for current function using creatinine and urine output trends; eGFR equations are not valid while creatinine is changing.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Creatinine and urea trend, sodium, potassium, bicarbonate or blood gas, calcium, phosphate, CBC with peripheral smear, LFTs, CK and glucose.
Urine dipstick and microscopy: muddy brown granular casts suggest tubular injury; red cell casts or dysmorphic red cells with proteinuria suggest glomerulonephritis.
Urine sodium or FeNa below 1% supports a prerenal state but is unreliable after diuretics and in sepsis, contrast AKI and CKD.
Renal ultrasound for hydronephrosis, kidney size (small echogenic kidneys suggest CKD) and asymmetry.

Tropical and environmental causes common in India: test for malaria, dengue, leptospirosis and scrub typhus; ask about snakebite, herbal or traditional remedies, diarrhoeal illness, heat exposure and pregnancy.
Suspected glomerulonephritis (haematuria, proteinuria, hypertension, rapid creatinine rise): ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, complement C3 and C4, and same-day nephrology referral for biopsy.

sections.title: Ongoing management
items: Use loop diuretics only for clinically significant volume overload, as intermittent IV boluses; do not use diuretics or low-dose dopamine to prevent or treat AKI itself.

Severe metabolic acidosis (pH below 7.20) without another urgent dialysis indication: IV sodium bicarbonate is suggested over dialysis (KDIGO 2026 draft); watch for volume overload and hypernatraemia.

Treat the cause: source control and antimicrobials in sepsis, relieve obstruction, stop the culprit drug in interstitial nephritis, disease-specific therapy for tropical infections, antivenom for envenomation.
Nutrition by the enteral route; do not restrict protein to delay dialysis. Limit potassium and phosphate intake when these are high.
If iodinated contrast is essential in a high-risk adult without fluid overload, give periprocedural IV 0.9% saline, use the lowest dose of low- or iso-osmolar contrast, and hold NSAIDs and diuretics.

sections.title: Urgent dialysis indications (AEIOU)
items: A: severe metabolic acidosis refractory to medical therapy.
E: hyperkalaemia refractory to medical treatment, especially 6.5 mmol/L or more or with ECG changes.
I: intoxication with a dialysable toxin such as lithium, methanol, ethylene glycol, salicylate, or metformin-associated lactic acidosis.
O: fluid overload or pulmonary oedema not responding to diuretics.
U: uraemic complications: pericarditis, encephalopathy, uraemic bleeding.
Without an urgent indication, deferred rather than early pre-emptive dialysis is recommended (KDIGO 2026 draft). If dialysis is likely, plan early transfer to a centre with nephrology and dialysis.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Hourly urine output in the critically ill (catheter only if needed for accurate measurement), daily weight and fluid balance.
Creatinine, urea, electrolytes and bicarbonate at least daily, more often in stage 2 to 3 or with hyperkalaemia.
Review the drug chart daily for dose changes, therapeutic drug levels (vancomycin, aminoglycosides) and a written restart plan for held drugs.

sections.title: Discharge and follow-up
items: Discharge summary should record the AKI episode, degree of recovery, drugs stopped and when to restart them, and the follow-up plan.
Restart RAS inhibitors after recovery when indicated, and reassess SGLT2 inhibitor and MRA; give sick day guidance.
Recheck creatinine and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 3 months after AKI to detect new or worsening CKD.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Assuming a normal first creatinine excludes AKI: creatinine lags behind the injury.
Missing obstruction or urinary retention, especially in older men and pelvic malignancy.
Repeated fluid boluses to an oliguric patient who is already euvolaemic or overloaded.
Missing rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis: an active urine sediment needs same-day nephrology input.
Continuing NSAIDs, ACE inhibitor or ARB, metformin or full-dose renally cleared antibiotics during AKI.

drugs.name: Buffered crystalloid (Ringer lactate, Plasma-Lyte)
drugs.dose: IV boluses of 250 to 500 mL with reassessment after each, for hypovolaemia
drugs.notes: Preferred over 0.9% saline for volume expansion (KDIGO 2026 draft); stop when no longer fluid responsive.

drugs.name: Furosemide
drugs.dose: 20 to 40 mg IV bolus initially, repeated or increased according to response
drugs.notes: Only for volume overload. Higher doses are often needed when GFR is low.

drugs.name: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)
drugs.dose: Start 0.05 to 0.1 mcg/kg/min IV, titrate to MAP above 65 mmHg

drugs.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
drugs.notes: For hyperkalaemia with ECG changes; see Hyperkalaemia protocol.
